Source: https://laravel.com/cloud/docs/pricing.md

# Plans and pricing

Learn about the plans, allowances, and usage-based pricing for Laravel Cloud.

## Plans

The **Starter plan** is perfect for kicking the tires and hosting small-scale, real-world applications. For \$5/mo, you get \$5 in monthly usage credits plus access to lightweight and cost-efficient compute, databases, and other resources. New Starter subscriptions get their first month free. Scale to zero is on by default, so you can preview and ship your code without the fear of a runaway bill. **Custom domains are included** too, so you have everything you need to ship your first apps to production right away.

As your applications scale up, you may need access to advanced features like autoscaling, high performance compute, dedicated worker clusters, edge security, and user and role management. When you're ready, upgrade to the **Growth** or **Business** plans to unlock the full range of Laravel Cloud's productivity, performance, and security features. Every paid plan includes \$5 in monthly usage credits, which apply to all usage and reset at the start of each billing period.

### Raising plan limits

On the Growth plan, you may [contact support](https://laravel.com/cloud/docs/support) to request an increase to the following limits without changing plans:

* App and worker cluster replicas (10 by default)
* Managed queue workers per queue (100 by default)
* Managed queues per environment (10 by default)
* Serverless Postgres compute units (4 CU by default)
* App compute, Laravel MySQL, Laravel Valkey, and managed queue sizes beyond those listed for your plan

Include your organization and environment, the limit you need, a description of your workload, and whether the increase is temporary or permanent. We may need to review available capacity before approving larger requests.

Standard usage-based rates still apply after a limit increase. If you are on the Starter plan, you must upgrade to Growth to request higher limits.

## Compute

Laravel Cloud applications run on the latest generation of AWS Graviton EC2 servers. Graviton's optimized cost-to-performance ratio lets us pass best-in-class compute performance and pricing on to you.

Laravel Cloud offers two classes of compute: Flex and Pro. Within each class, there are multiple sizes of CPU and RAM available.

> [card] Flex
>
> Lightweight and cost-efficient. Scales to zero and wakes up in under 500 milliseconds. Perfect for smaller apps that have periods of inactivity.

> [card] Pro
>
> Higher-performance compute for sustained, heavy use. Best for large-scale, always-on production applications.

> [!TIP]
>
> Enable [scale to zero](https://laravel.com/cloud/docs/compute#scale-to-zero) on your latency-tolerant environments to save even more on compute.

### Compute sizes

\* Accrued for each second an instance runs. See [How bandwidth allowances work](#how-bandwidth-allowances-work).

### How compute billing works

Laravel Cloud bills compute usage pro rata for each second a replica in an App or worker cluster is running. To keep your compute spend consistent and predictable, Cloud bills each replica for a maximum of 28 days (2,419,200 seconds) every billing period.

## Bandwidth

Each Cloud environment includes an allowance of [free data transfer](#compute-sizes). Additional data transfer costs \$0.10 per GB. We set these allowances well above the average usage of most applications at each compute size, so most Cloud users never incur bandwidth overage charges.

### How bandwidth allowances work

For every second a compute instance is running, Laravel Cloud credits your organization with a proportional amount of data transfer allowance.

For example, a `Flex 1GiB RAM` instance earns 100GB of data transfer allowance per month, which is equivalent to about 0.000041GB (41KB) per second.

If multiple instances (replicas) are running in a compute cluster, the data transfer allowance earned per second is multiplied by the number of running instances.

Unused data transfer allowances reset at the end of each billing period.

### Sharing bandwidth allowances across environments

Data transfer allowances are shared across all environments and applications within your Cloud organization.

**Example:** If Environment A earns 500GB and uses 100GB, while Environment B earns 500GB and uses 800GB:

* **Total allowance:** 1,000GB (1TB)
* **Total usage:** 900GB
* **Remaining:** 100GB (no overage charges)

Spiky traffic may cause your [Allowances](https://laravel.com/to/org/usage/allowances) summary to temporarily estimate a data transfer overage. However, Laravel Cloud doesn't apply overage charges until the end of the billing period, after your organization has accrued all of its data transfer allowances.

### Calculating bandwidth usage

* What's included: cached data returned from the [Edge Network](https://laravel.com/cloud/docs/network#cloud-edge-network), incoming request and response data served by your applications in the [Compute Network](https://laravel.com/cloud/docs/network#cloud-compute-network), and outgoing request and response data when your application makes an external connection to a database, API, or other services.
* What's excluded: internal data transfers that take place within the Cloud Network.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Laravel MySQL, Laravel Reverb, and Laravel Valkey are hosted within the Cloud Network and qualify as internal data transfers. Partners manage all other resources, so data transfer to those resources counts as external. See [Resources](#resources) for more details.

## Resources

Applications often use additional resources like databases, caches, or object storage buckets. Laravel Cloud offers first-party support for the following resources:

### Laravel MySQL

A managed MySQL database with scalable compute and storage plus daily backups. Flex sizes can [scale to zero](https://laravel.com/cloud/docs/resources/databases/laravel-mysql#scale-to-zero) when idle, and are available in all regions.

Laravel MySQL offers two classes of compute:

> [card] Flex
>
> Lightweight and cost-efficient. Perfect for small databases that need the flexibility to support periodic bursts in traffic.

> [card] Pro
>
> Higher-performance compute for sustained, heavy use. Best for large-scale, mission-critical workloads.

Laravel Cloud bills Laravel MySQL compute for each second the database cluster is awake, up to the monthly cap. Flex clusters that [scale to zero](https://laravel.com/cloud/docs/resources/databases/laravel-mysql#scale-to-zero) don't incur compute charges while they sleep. Storage and backups are billed continuously, including while a database sleeps.

**Plan limitations:** Starter plan users can use only `flex` compute sizes, while Growth and Business plan users can use both `flex` and `pro` compute sizes. Growth plan users who need a size beyond their plan may [request an increase](#raising-plan-limits).

### Serverless Postgres

A managed, serverless PostgreSQL database powered by [Neon](https://neon.tech) that includes scale to zero, autoscaling, and point-in-time recovery.

<table><thead><tr><th>Metric</th>
<th>Price</th>
<th>Note</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>CPU</td>
<td>$ per hour</td>                     <td>Billed per second of active compute usage.</td></tr>                 <tr><td>Storage</td>                     <td>$ per GB-mo</td>
<td>Total volume of database disk usage.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Backup History</td>
<td>\$ per GB-mo</td>
<td>Total volume of Point-in-Time Restore logs within your backup window.</td></tr></tbody></table>

Laravel Cloud bills Serverless Postgres database clusters to the second for the time they are active and not sleeping, regardless of query activity. Any database query or transaction restarts the delay before the cluster scales to zero.

> [!TIP]
>
> Pair a Laravel Serverless Postgres database cluster that scales to zero with application compute that scales to zero to minimize costs on your dev environments or side projects.

**Plan limitations:**

* **Starter**: Up to 1 CU
* **Growth**: Up to 4 CU by default ([request a higher limit](#raising-plan-limits))
* **Business**: Up to 10 CU

### Laravel Valkey

A managed, Redis-compatible cache for caching, queueing, sessions, and other application data. Laravel applications can use it as a cache, queue, or session driver.

### Managed queues

Fully managed queues with dedicated workers that scale with the jobs waiting to be processed. Managed queues include a built-in failed jobs dashboard.

Managed queues offer two classes of compute:

> [card] Flex
>
> Scales to zero when idle and wakes in under a second. Perfect for spiky or idle-heavy workloads.

> [card] Pro
>
> Always on, with larger sizes and no fixed limit on job runtime. Best for steady throughput and long-running jobs.

**Plan limitations:** Starter plan users are limited to Flex sizes, while Growth, Business, and Enterprise plan users can use both Flex and Pro sizes. On the Growth plan, managed queue sizes, workers per queue, and queues per environment may be [raised on request](#raising-plan-limits).

See [Managed queues](https://laravel.com/cloud/docs/queues#pricing) for billing details, plan limits, and workload guidance.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Redis by Upstash is deprecated.** You can no longer create new caches. The new prices take effect on **November 30, 2026**. Laravel Cloud will sunset Redis by Upstash on **August 31, 2027**.
>
> Beginning **October 1, 2026**, Upstash also enforces the monthly data transfer allowance listed for each cache size. Caches with auto-upgrade enabled move to the next size when they use up their allowance. Caches with auto-upgrade disabled stop accepting connections until the next calendar month begins or you resize the cache. See [Bandwidth limits and auto-upgrades](https://laravel.com/cloud/docs/resources/caches/redis#bandwidth-limits-and-auto-upgrades) for details.
>
> We recommend migrating to [Laravel Valkey](https://laravel.com/cloud/docs/resources/caches/valkey), which offers Redis API compatibility, better performance, and more precise per-second billing. Follow the [migration guide](https://laravel.com/cloud/docs/knowledge-base/migrate-upstash-to-valkey) to move your cache, sessions, queues, and Redis data. If you need a larger cache, managed AWS [ElastiCache](https://laravel.com/cloud/docs/private-cloud/elasticache) caches are available to Enterprise customers. [Contact sales](https://laravel.com/cloud/contact) to learn more.

Each message received from a client and each message sent to a client counts separately toward the daily message allowance. For example, a server broadcast delivered to 100 subscribers counts as 100 messages. Connection, subscription, and presence messages count, along with `pusher:ping` and `pusher:pong` messages. Native WebSocket ping and pong control frames do not count.

## Example scenarios

The best way to understand Cloud pricing is to see it applied to real applications. The estimates below use **US East (Ohio)** pricing over a 30-day month, with hourly rates derived from the per-second [compute](#compute-sizes) and resource prices for readability. Always-on resources cap at 28 days (672 hours) per billing period. Every plan includes \$5 in monthly usage credits that these totals do not subtract, so your actual bill is often lower.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Flex compute, Serverless Postgres, and Flex-sized Laravel Valkey caches all [scale to zero](https://laravel.com/cloud/docs/compute#scale-to-zero) when idle and wake in well under a second. Latency-tolerant and bursty workloads pay only for the hours they are running.

### Side project

A score tracker for a local pub quiz with around 30 users that runs a few times a month and sleeps the rest of the time. With scale to zero enabled on both compute and the database, the entire application costs pennies to run.

| Line item | Calculation | Monthly est. |
| - | - | - |
| Flex 512MB compute | 4 hrs × \$0.00893/hr | \$0.04 |
| Serverless Postgres compute (0.25 vCPU) | 4 hrs × \$0.106/hr × 0.25 | \$0.11 |
| Serverless Postgres storage | 0.5 GB × \$0.50/GB | \$0.25 |
| **Total** | | **\~\$0.40** |

That total sits comfortably inside the \$5 monthly usage credit, so the effective compute and database cost is \$0.

### Small blog or content site

A content site with a few thousand monthly readers and a newsletter signup. The [Edge Network](https://laravel.com/cloud/docs/network#cloud-edge-network) cache serves static pages, so compute wakes only to process a form submission or render a page that has not been cached yet.

| Line item | Calculation | Monthly est. |
| - | - | - |
| Flex 1GB compute | 60 hrs × \$0.01786/hr | \$1.07 |
| Serverless Postgres compute (0.25 vCPU) | 60 hrs × \$0.106/hr × 0.25 | \$1.59 |
| Serverless Postgres storage | 5 GB × \$0.50/GB | \$2.50 |
| Laravel Valkey 250MB (Flex) | 60 hrs × \$0.00893/hr | \$0.54 |
| **Total** | | **\~\$5.70** |

Edge caching keeps compute asleep through the long tail of idle hours. Scale to zero on the database and cache means you pay only when a reader triggers a query.

### Medium SaaS application

A Laravel or Symfony SaaS application with a few hundred monthly users, quiet on nights and weekends, with background jobs handled by a [managed queue](https://laravel.com/cloud/docs/queues#managed-queues). Compute scales to zero off-hours, while the database stays on so data is always available.

| Line item | Calculation | Monthly est. |
| - | - | - |
| Flex 2GB compute (primary) | 365 hrs × \$0.03571/hr | \$13.04 |
| Flex 2GB compute (autoscaled) | 73 hrs × \$0.03571/hr | \$2.61 |
| Laravel MySQL Flex 2GB compute | 672 hrs (capped) × \$0.03274/hr | \$22.00 |
| Laravel MySQL storage | 20 GB × \$0.10/GB | \$2.00 |
| Laravel Valkey 1GB (Flex) | 365 hrs × \$0.03571/hr | \$13.04 |
| Managed queue workers (Flex 256 MiB) | \~40 worker-hrs × \$0.00548/hr | \$0.22 |
| Managed queue operations | \~1M ops × \$1.00/1M | \$1.00 |
| **Total** | | **\~\$53.90** |

The managed queue replaces a dedicated worker entirely. Workers scale up only while jobs are waiting and back to zero when the queue drains, so background processing costs about \$1, far less than running an always-on worker around the clock.

### High-traffic e-commerce store or consumer SaaS

A Laravel or Symfony ecommerce store or consumer SaaS that runs around the clock. Three always-on replicas keep it available under load, and a [managed queue](https://laravel.com/cloud/docs/queues#managed-queues) absorbs continuous job volume. The queue scales out during spikes instead of running idle workers.

| Line item | Calculation | Monthly est. |
| - | - | - |
| Pro 4GB compute | 672 hrs (capped) × \$0.04762/hr × 3 replicas | \$96.00 |
| Laravel MySQL Pro 4GB compute | 672 hrs (capped) × \$0.07143/hr | \$48.00 |
| Laravel MySQL storage | 40 GB × \$0.10/GB | \$4.00 |
| Laravel Valkey 2.5GB (Flex) | 672 hrs (capped) × \$0.07143/hr | \$48.00 |
| Managed queue workers (Flex 512 MiB) | \~730 worker-hrs × \$0.01096/hr | \$8.00 |
| Managed queue operations | \~15.5M ops × \$1.00/1M | \$15.50 |

Always-on Pro compute and matching resources deliver consistent performance. The managed queue scales workers with queue pressure, so you pay for processing rather than idle capacity.
